hypothesis_candidates.hypothesis: A date-native all-market candidate pool that includes later-delisted securities may expose liquid continuation opportunities omitted by the legacy core roster.
hypothesis_candidates.treatment: fixed outcome-blind broad continuation policy over date-native Massive membership
hypothesis_candidates.falsifier: after costs, replacement value is nonpositive, unstable across fixed windows, or dominated by concentration

hypothesis_candidates.hypothesis: Survivorship-safe membership changes the measured breadth and opportunity cost of the already fixed broad-market paper rule.
hypothesis_candidates.treatment: same frozen rule on Massive date-native rows

hypothesis_candidates.hypothesis: Replacing core identity priority with liquidity and signal strength may improve slot allocation without raising concentration.
hypothesis_candidates.falsifier: incremental replacement value versus displaced core/cash is nonpositive

selected_hypothesis: Build the Massive date-native full-market research surface first; do not select or test a winner until the source artifact and D0-D3 panel are frozen.
economic_mechanism: The legacy core/current-roster surface omits securities that later delisted or were acquired, biasing both opportunity counts and historical winner selection; date-native traded rows remove that identity prior before any return is inspected.
falsifier: Authorization, timestamp, identity, split, provenance, coverage, or reproducibility contract fails before outcomes are read.
